clue.text: Change into suit

definitions.meaning: to change into something is to turn into it, as a caterpillar does a butterfly
to suit someone is to look good on them, as a colour flatters

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get dressed in a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are verbs: to turn into (a frog that will be a prince) and to flatter in appearance (that hat really flatters you).

clue.text: Bishop smuggled guerrilla's arms

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to run goods is to smuggle them
Che Guevara was the famous guerrilla leader, so the guerrilla's is CHE'S

explanation.surface: A bishop sneaked weapons to the guerrillas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' looks like weapons; it means limbs of a tree or offshoots.
explanation.definitionFit: The limbs of a tree, river or organisation, its offshoots, are its arms.

clue.text: In Manila, leading man jumps into bed

indicators.note: to jump into is to go inside, so the leading man goes within the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
the hero is the leading man of a film or play

explanation.surface: In the Philippine capital a film star leaps into bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manila' looks like the city; it is a cigar from there.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manila is a cigar from the Philippines, and a cheroot is a cigar with both ends cut.

clue.text: Principal bottles up rebuke to a pupil appearing early

indicators.note: to bottle up is to hold inside, so principal encloses the rebuke

parts.note: main means principal or chief
tut is an exclamation of rebuke
L is a learner, the pupil of a driving test

explanation.surface: A head teacher keeps a telling-off for a pupil who arrives early.
explanation.definitionFit: Matutinal means of the morning, so active or seen in the early hours.

clue.text: I am permitted to accept money, that's understood

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the first pieces open up and hold the money

parts.note: contracted, I am is I'M
licit means lawful or permitted
P is penny, a small coin of money

explanation.surface: Someone allowed to take payment says it goes without saying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is not stated but tacitly grasped, so it is understood without words.

clue.text: Doting mum keeps on, and I reach a decision

indicators.note: doting suggests muddled or senile, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fond mother keeps nagging until the speaker decides.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle firmly on a course is to make a decision, so the idiom means to decide.

clue.text: Stop rent increase

parts.note: to let is to rent out
up means an increase, as in a price going up

explanation.surface: A demand to halt a rise in rents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' must be read as a noun, a pause or easing off.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause or easing off is a break, so a let-up is a stop.

clue.text: A note; formerly, it was a crotchet

parts.note: C is a musical note
once means formerly, at one time

explanation.surface: A music lesson on how a quarter note used to be named.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crotchet' looks like the musical quarter note; it is the old word for a whim or odd notion.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is an odd fancy or whim, and a conceit is a fanciful notion.

clue.text: Where kings are seated and unseated, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase says the word is judged by how it is heard

parts.note: a rider unseated from a horse has been thrown

explanation.surface: Monarchs sit here and are toppled, so it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's ceremonial chair is the seat of royal power.

clue.text: Abandoned wife — send her eau de Cologne — a valediction

definitions.note: French 'de' means 'of', so this is a farewell of the German city

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so these letters run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A deserted wife is sent perfume as a parting gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eau de Cologne' reads as one phrase, but 'eau' is fodder and 'de Cologne' joins the definition: a farewell from Cologne, so in German.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the German phrase for goodbye, literally until we see again, a farewell as used in Cologne.

clue.text: Impressed by a number of points in connection with the business

parts.note: W, E and S are three of the compass points: west, east and south
truck is old-fashioned for dealings, as in 'have no truck with'

explanation.surface: Someone is struck by how many points are scored in a business deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be awestruck is to be filled with wonder, deeply moved or overcome.

clue.text: In a quite normal voice

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the words that follow, so they are found within them

explanation.surface: Someone speaks at an ordinary level.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor is a male singing voice, the highest in ordinary use.

clue.text: A quid a month brought in by Indian

indicators.note: the month is taken inside, carried in by the quid

parts.note: a quid is a lump of chewing tobacco, also called a chaw
Oct is October, a month

explanation.surface: A Native American is paid a pound every month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quid' looks like a British pound; here it is a wad of tobacco. 'Indian' is a Native American: the Choctaw are a people of the south-eastern US.
explanation.definitionFit: The Choctaw are a Native American people, so a member is an American Indian in the old wording.

clue.text: Many men put out about end of affaire

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the last letter
put out suggests disturbed, so these letters are thrown into a new order
end of picks the final letter of the word affaire

explanation.surface: Men are upset by how their love affair finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' reads as upset, but only 'out' signals the shuffle; 'about' wraps the shuffled UMPTEN round the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteen is informal for a great number, used for countless or very many.

clue.text: Taken in school — oral

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so it is the sound of the school's name that counts

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school near Windsor

explanation.surface: Something learned at school in a spoken lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON College is an exclusive English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Food taken in has been swallowed and consumed.

clue.text: Stretch in solitary for concealing gun after completion of crime

indicators.note: the completion of a word is its final letter, here of crime
concealing means hiding inside, so the gun goes within solitary

parts.note: lone means solitary, on one's own
gat is old slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A prisoner serves a stretch in solitary for hiding a gun after a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the E of crime first. 'Stretch' and 'solitary' suggest prison time, but the definition is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen something is to draw it out, so to stretch it.

clue.text: Composite set comprises several games

indicators.note: to comprise is to contain, so set holds the games inside it

parts.note: to gel is to set, as a jelly does
rounds are separate games, as of golf

explanation.surface: A collection is made up of several games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composite' looks like an adjective; botanists use it for a plant of the daisy family, to which groundsel, a common weed, belongs.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundsel is a weed of the daisy family, whose members botanists call composites.

clue.text: Pear-tree could make a come-back

indicators.note: could make says these letters can be made into something new by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A pear tree might recover and grow again.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is a quick witty reply, so a smart retort or comeback.

clue.text: Gold from the mint

definitions.meaning: the gold is the centre of an archery target
a hard round peppermint sweet with stripes goes by this name in Britain

explanation.surface: Precious metal fresh from where coins are struck.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is also a striped peppermint sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden inner ring of an archery target is the bull, and a striped boiled peppermint sweet carries the same name.

clue.text: Keen, outstanding person turned up and dined

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a lulu is informal for a remarkable person or thing
ate means dined

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic star guest arrives and has dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager; it is the verb to wail in mourning.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in grief, and to ululate is to howl or wail.

clue.text: Speaking of Christmas, I'll provide for the next generation

definitions.text: I'll provide for the next generation

indicators.note: speaking means said aloud, so the words are heard as a single word

parts.note: Yule is an old name for Christmas, so of Christmas is 'o' Yule'

explanation.surface: Talk of Christmas prompts a promise to look after the young.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovule is the structure in a plant that becomes a seed after fertilisation, so it supplies offspring.

clue.text: Honourable and noted music-maker

definitions.meaning: a piano with vertical strings is a music-maker that plays notes

explanation.surface: A respectable and famous musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' is a pun: famous, and producing notes.
explanation.definitionFit: An honest person is upright, and an upright is a vertical piano that sounds notes.

clue.text: A bank out of touch

parts.note: a drift is a bank of snow or sand

explanation.surface: A bank has lost contact with its customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a financial firm; it is a heap of snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cut off from contact or direction, one is drifting and lost.

clue.text: U.S.A. gold rebuilt island capital

indicators.note: rebuilt means put together again differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: American gold is used to rebuild a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief town of the Isle of Man is Douglas, so it is an island's capital.

clue.text: Better counsel wife to leave

indicators.note: to leave means to go away, so the wife's letter is dropped

parts.note: a counsel in court is a lawyer

explanation.surface: Advice for a wife to walk out would be an improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like an adjective; it is one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer is one who lays odds or bets, so a bettor.

clue.text: Pitman's books about deity

parts.note: a pitman is a coal miner

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible, a set of books

explanation.surface: A coal miner's library is described as being about a god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitman' suggests Isaac Pitman of shorthand fame; here it is simply a coal miner.
explanation.definitionFit: Minerva is the Roman goddess of wisdom.

clue.text: In the autumn London yuppy heads for the country

indicators.note: heads are the leading letters of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: Come autumn, young London professionals head off into the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' looks like rural land; it is a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is a European nation.

clue.text: It helps in shooting deer — a lot

parts.note: a hind is a female red deer
a sight is informal for a great deal, as in 'a sight better'

explanation.surface: Something is useful for a hunter after deer, a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: A hindsight is the rear sight on a gun barrel, which helps one aim; the usual sense of wisdom after the event is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm's rear sight is named this way, and aligning it with the foresight is how a shooter aims.

clue.text: Other people catch trains, in the main

indicators.note: to catch is to hold, so the outer piece holds the rest

parts.note: they means other people
BR is British Rail, the old national train company

explanation.surface: Commuters catch trains for their main journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is old poetic wording for the sea. BR was British Rail.
explanation.definitionFit: The briny is informal for the sea, which poets call the main.

clue.text: Sails finally subside to deck

parts.note: sails are made of cloth, canvas

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word subside

explanation.surface: A ship's sails finally collapse onto the deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like a ship's deck; it is the verb to dress up.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck someone out is to dress or adorn them.
